title: Ephemeral on-call primer generator and telemetry credentialing
author: Sofia Ramirez
description:
Motivation: On-call handoffs frequently lack a concise starter context for the incoming responder. Existing runbook links are useful but noisy: responders need a compact, reproducible primer that bundles sanitized telemetry, quick triage hints, and ephemeral access tokens for pinned artifacts. This PR implements a lightweight "on-call primer" generator (service + CLI) that packages a short incident summary, a prioritized list of diagnostic commands, a clipped telemetry bundle (logs/traces/metrics subset), and short-lived credential artifacts to access attachments. The generator aims to reduce time-to-first-action and avoid leaking permanent credentials.

What this PR does: Adds a new slo-toolkit subservice (primer) and CLI command: `slo primer create` which: generates a one-page primer in markdown, collects and sanitizes a telemetry bundle (configurable time window and sampling budget), creates ephemeral signed URLs and short-lived tokens for attachments (rotated on handoff), and attaches safe guidance snippets (service runbook pointers plus two actionable next steps). The implementation includes: - Primer generation engine and templating - Telemetry clipping/sanitizer with redaction rules and size budget enforcement - Ephemeral credential manager with TTLs and rotation hooks - Integration with incident-bot handoff webhook (optional) - Unit and e2e tests + local dev harness and docs.

Security model: telemetry sanitzation runs through a configurable rule set (regex-based and allowlist for keys). Attachment URLs are implemented as time-limited signed URLs backed by the existing attachment-store service; tokens are short-lived (default 10 minutes) and revokable. The design intentionally avoids storing permanent secrets; ephemeral credentials are issued on-demand and recorded in the handoff event for audit.

Testing and rollout: Added comprehensive unit tests for sanitization rules and credential lifecycle; added an e2e test that exercises the incident-bot -> primer -> handoff flow using a local mock attachment-store. CI passes lint/build/unit; added a canary rollout plan: enable in non-prod incident channels for 48h, gather usage metrics (latency, primer size, token issuance rate) and a small oncall survey for usefulness.

Backward compatibility and opt-in: Feature is opt-in via a per-channel toggle in incident-bot. If disabled, incident-bot handoffs behave as before. Default toggles are off for enterprise/private installations until security review completes.

Notes on implementation constraints: Telemetry clipping enforces both time-window and byte budget; if clipped, the primer includes an explicit "clipped: true" section with instructions for requesting full artifacts (via standard escalation). The token issuance respects org policy (max tokens per minute) and will fallback to signed URL-only mode if token service is rate-limited.

References: Linear ENG-2319 for product ask, security checklist in docs/security/primer-security.md.

Rollback: Feature gate and a quick toggle in incident-bot allow turning off primer generation immediately; tokens already issued will be auto-expired per TTL.

This description is intentionally compact but covers implementation, security posture, test coverage, and rollout plan.
commits: init: add primer service scaffold and CLI
feat(primer): telemetry clipper and sanitizer with rule engine
feat(credentials): ephemeral token and signed-URL integration
chore(tests): add unit + e2e harness for primer flow
docs: primer usage, security model, and rollout notes
fix(sanitizer): more conservative redaction for user identifiers
perf: stream telemetry packager to reduce memory spikes
review_conversation: Jordan Park: Nice direction. Please make sure the sanitizer rejects PII by default and we log sanitized keys only. Can we add a summary hash so recipients can verify they saw the same telemetry?
Sofia Ramirez (author): Added a content-hash field to the primer; sanitizer defaults to deny-list PII patterns and publishes the sanitized-keyset to audit logs. See sanitizer.py lines 120-190.
Ellen Nguyen: Security requested a change: tokens should be single-use where possible to reduce replay risk. Also add an ACL check on signed URLs so we don't accidentally leak private attachments.
Sofia Ramirez (author): Updated credentials manager to emit single-use short-lived tokens and attached an ACL check step. Documented fallback to signed-URL-only flow when ACLs prevent token issuance.
Ravi Desai: Perf nit — streaming packager can OOM on large traces, can we stream to disk when > 50MB?
Sofia Ramirez (author): Implemented streaming buffer with ephemeral disk spill; added unit test to simulate 120MB trace and verified memory usage under threshold.
Security Team (via Ellen): Reviewed primer-security.md and gave conditional approval pending a brief run in staging and a short security audit of sanitizer rules.
Ops: Verified the handoff webhook integration in staging and confirmed toggle works; will enable in non-prod channels for canary.
release_notes: Adds an opt-in on-call primer generator that packages sanitized telemetry and ephemeral credentials for handoffs; includes CLI and incident-bot integration; default off for enterprise until security review is complete.
